CONGRANT.TITLE: CISE MSI: RPEP: CPS: Trustworthy AI for Transportation Cyber-Physical Systems
CREST Center for Multidisciplinary Research Excellence in Cyber-Physical Infrastructure Systems (MECIS)
CONGRANT.ABSTRACT:
Overview:
The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV) proposes to establish the “CREST Center for Multidisciplinary Research Excellence in Cyber-Physical Infrastructure Systems (MECIS).” The Center’s mission is to advance and transform the much-needed research and education at the nexus of automation, sensors, and artificial intelligence (AI), as integral parts of the “NSF’s 10 Big Ideas,” anticipating the revolutionary cyber-physical infrastructure systems (CIS). Three Colleges of Engineering, Sciences, and Education at UTRGV in collaboration with the Universities of Illinois (at Urbana-Champaign and at Chicago) and California (Riverside) will pursue multidisciplinary research on CIS, aiming to: (i) transfer technology to various transportation, logistics, manufacturing, and construction industries; and (ii) prepare a minority STEM workforce to drive future CIS-based communities. The Center envisions a portfolio of three research subprojects on automation, sensors, and AI that bridges diverse STEM disciplines. A holistic, multi-level approach is adopted to address CIS planning, design, and operation. While each subproject constitutes a unique element, their synergy ensures the CIS integrity.
Subproject 1 pushes the frontiers of knowledge in future transportation infrastructure, which will be transformed by autonomous vehicles (AVs) and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), in six directions: (i) at the planning level, public acceptance and policy issues of (U)AV; (ii-iv) at the design level, computer vision, automatic navigation, and model/field-based testing of the designed capabilities; and (v, vi) at the operation level, human-(U)AV interactions and network-wide inter-(U)AV interactions.
Subproject 2 designs and embeds sensors in CIS for two purposes. First, (U)AV sensors help perform automated tasks. Second, sensors in civil infrastructure and (U)AVs monitor infrastructure health. Three research areas are defined: (i, ii) at the design level, computational simulation, synthesis, and 3D printing of sensor materials and UAV structures, and (iii) at the operation level, cost-effective decision-making to upkeep infrastructure health using sensor data.
Since (U)AVs and sensors will inherently generate big data, Subproject 3 will synchronously work with subprojects 1 and 2 to: (i) develop AI solutions for big data management, and (ii) develop AI algorithms for big data analytics and decision making in the design and operation of (U)AVs and infrastructure.
UTRGV is the nation’s second largest Hispanic-Serving Institute (HIS) located in South Texas with an established record of preparing underrepresented minority students for STEM careers. The Center will provide (under)graduate students with cutting-edge CIS research experience, will integrate CIS research and education, and will pave a pathway from High School through graduate programs in STEM disciplines. This broad initiative at UTRGV will also offer new courses related to the subprojects. The Center will further enhance the research infrastructure at UTRGV and will strengthen the research competitiveness of a diverse group of faculty.
Intellectual Merit:
The proposed self-sustaining Center will play a key role in transforming the scientific discoveries at the intersection of automation, sensors, and AI technologies, which are the integral elements of next-generation CIS. The Center will address current gaps in the planning, design, and operation of CIS by proposing innovative theoretical, computational, experimental, and empirical solutions spanning from micro (molecule)- to macro (system)-scale, which also yield practical solutions valuable for the industry.
Broader Impacts:
The Center’s research and education activities will develop an underrepresented workforce equipped with the skills to address complex societal problems. The Center will partner with the public and private sectors to advance technology transfer and product development in CIS. The Center’s activities are key for the establishment of an inaugural engineering doctoral program, which will be vital in elevating UTRGV to a Research I institution and advancing the CIS research agenda in a predominantly HSI. The Center's research findings will be made available to the research community as journal publications and conference proceedings, which will inform other domains undergoing related transformations, such as the health industry, manufacturing and production systems, and the military.
